question: How often does a training batch of 32 contain a semantically equivalent report pair that InfoNCE then pushes apart, and is there a similarity source that identifies such pairs reliably?

e5_full_report.how: frozen intfloat/multilingual-e5-base rev d1287505, 'query: ' prefix, mean pooling, 512 tokens - exactly the text tower the arms would use
e5_full_report.verdict: UNUSABLE as a false-negative detector. Similarity is dominated by the shared structured template, not by findings: a Morel-Lavallee hematoma and a patellofemoral maltracking report sit at 0.9912, while the median pair is 0.889. Only above ~0.995 are pairs genuinely equivalent, and that is 0.19 expected collisions per batch.

tfidf.how: sublinear TF-IDF, 1-2 grams, min_df=3, max_df=0.5; document frequency discounts the template
tfidf.verdict: Behaves correctly - pairs above 0.90 are genuinely equivalent by reading, pairs at 0.80 are not - but genuine duplicates are RARE: 0.10 expected collisions per batch of 32, i.e. ~9% of batches contain one, one pair in 496.

conclusion.fnc: NOT SUPPORTED at batch 32. The only similarity source that identifies genuine duplicates (TF-IDF) finds ~0.1 per batch. Masking one pair in 496 cannot move a 3-seed result, and the source that would fire often enough (full-report e5) fires on unrelated findings.
conclusion.soft_targets: NOT SUPPORTED either. At most 3% of off-diagonal target mass reaches a genuine duplicate at any setting large enough to matter. Both forms fail for the same reason: at batch 32 there is almost nothing to fix. Batch size, not target shape, is the binding constraint.

soft_target_mass_attribution.how: 600 random batches of 32; share of all off-diagonal target mass landing on TF-IDF>0.90 pairs
soft_target_mass_attribution.verdict: Sharpening trades one failure for another. Loose settings put target mass on true negatives; the one well-aimed setting moves 0.26% of total target mass. Soft targets degenerate to uniform label smoothing at this duplicate rate.
